To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the serum cystatin C level, a marker of renal function, was independently associated with LV mass and left atrial diameter in a cohort of patients with HF.
serum cystatin C levels are associated with LV mass index (LVMi) and left atrial (LA) size in a general population.

serum cystatin C levels, an independent marker of renal function, are associated with the presence of left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) in the absence of diabetes and that the presence of LVH is associated with the development of HF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of renal filtration function and serum cystatin C in the development and progression of heart failure.
the role that renal dysfunction plays in the development of LV remodeling and heart failure.
the development of new and innovative methods of treatment and prevention for heart failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the actual prevalence of HF is unknown.
the prevalence of LV dysfunction is unknown, but it may be as high as 20 million people.3
HF is a clinical syndrome that can result from any structural or functional cardiac disorder that impairs the ability of the ventricle to fill with or eject blood.3
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cystatin C is a better marker for renal function than creatinine and that the cystatin C/creatinine ratio is associated with LV hypertrophy and remodeling.
the use of serum cystatin C (sCysC) is a useful tool in the evaluation of renal filtration function in HF.
the prevalence of HF is much greater than previously recognized.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of serum cystatin C, a novel biomarker of renal filtration function, in combination with the traditional markers of renal function, creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), may help to better define the relationship between renal dysfunction and LV remodeling.
the use of a novel marker of renal filtration function may be helpful in identifying patients with HF at high risk for LV remodeling.
serum cystatin C, an emerging marker for renal filtration function, is a strong predictor of LV mass and LV hypertrophy.
